milestone: Brownie Runtime Release Readiness P0/P1 Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Allows the release readiness audit to converge from open Runtime P0/P1 blockers to closed evidence without rewriting the guard every phase.
Keeps autonomous phase selection finite by making the guard validate the audit state instead of hard-coding only the current incomplete state.
Preserves Runtime-owned release blockers and prevents closed or external items from remaining release blockers.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement and headless_autonomous_development, with controlled_workspace_tools protected by the same release gate.
answers.new_capability: The Runtime release readiness guard can now validate both the current not-ready audit state and the future terminal ready state after all Runtime P0/P1 release blockers are closed.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: The guard already accepted current incomplete evidence, but it fixed required Runtime blocker debt to required_before_release and runtime_release_ready=false, so later closure phases would have to rewrite guard source to mark blockers closed.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: MCP-S2 and later release phases could implement real closure evidence yet fail the release guard merely because the guard cannot represent convergence.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes the guard's machine-checkable acceptance semantics and tests terminal convergence; it does not add another report, wrapper, endpoint, or MCP execution surface.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths are preserved.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase updates an existing release guard and audit artifact, not a new user-facing summary API.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Open Runtime P0/P1 required-before-release items still force runtime_release_ready=false, closed Runtime items must use implemented_sufficient plus closed, closed items cannot remain in release_ready_blocked_by, and an all-closed Runtime audit must set runtime_release_ready=true.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The loop can now close Runtime release blockers one by one without creating a fresh guard-source corrective for every successful phase.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the guard convergence blocker recorded before MCP-S2 while leaving the remaining MCP-S2 through MCP-S7 safety work open.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRG-1 updates the Runtime Release Readiness guard, so strict review must verify that convergence support cannot mask open Runtime release blockers, leave closed blockers in release_ready_blocked_by, or convert excluded platform/product work into Runtime release scope.

exit_criteria: Current incomplete Runtime release audit still passes with runtime_release_ready=false while Runtime P0/P1 blockers remain open.
A terminal audit with all Runtime P0/P1 blockers implemented_sufficient and closed passes with runtime_release_ready=true.
Open Runtime P0/P1 release blockers must be present in release_ready_blocked_by.
Closed, unknown, owner, and external items cannot remain in release_ready_blocked_by.
Runtime-owned P0/P1 items cannot be misclassified as external post-v0 debt.
The remaining CI workflow hardening blocker stays partial and required_before_release.
behavior_evidence: pnpm guard:runtime-release-readiness:test covers current not-ready acceptance, terminal ready acceptance, stale not-ready rejection, and closed blocker rejection.
pnpm guard:runtime-release-readiness validates the current Runtime Release Readiness audit.
docs/architecture/runtime-release-readiness-audit.json records guard convergence evidence while keeping full CI workflow hardening open.

accepted_capability: Runtime Release Readiness guard now supports bounded open-to-closed blocker convergence.
Runtime Release Ready can become true only after all Runtime P0/P1 release blockers are implemented_sufficient and closed.
behavior_evidence: Runtime release readiness guard tests cover current not-ready audits, terminal ready audits, stale not-ready terminal audits, and closed blockers left in release_ready_blocked_by.
The current Runtime Release Readiness audit still passes while existing Runtime blockers remain open.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
The guard validates audit-owned release readiness evidence; prose, CLI, VSIX, AgentModes, MCP metadata, and external artifacts cannot grant release readiness.
External platform, adapter, commercial, scheduler, daemon, registry, and hosted features remain outside Runtime release blockers.
non_goals: Does not add a Brownie-specific tool adapter SDK or protocol.

Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, public registry, automatic install, scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or recursive Brownie invocation.
Does not close MCP-S2 through MCP-S7.
Does not close full CI workflow hardening while workflow update authority is unavailable.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected leaving runtime_release_ready hard-coded to false because it prevents finite release convergence.
Rejected letting closed Runtime items remain in release_ready_blocked_by because that would hide stale audit state.
Rejected broad CI workflow changes because workflow update authority remains unavailable in this environment.
